title: Anchored IO parity banding & enterprise-SQ harmonization for Hosted API pricing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Hypothesis: Introducing an anchored per-session IO parity band (a bounded input/output delta band) plus an enterprise SQ-ready disclosure and playbook will reduce billing disputes by >=30% for enterprise customers while preserving net hosted revenue and keeping end-to-end latency/regression risk negligible.

Experiment design: 1) Define parity band: for each session we compute ingress tokens and egress tokens. If |egress - ingress| <= band (initial band = 1.25x egress-to-ingress), no extra minimum applies. Outside the band we apply an anchored adjustment (small premium on heavy-output sessions) with a capped per-session minimum. 2) Support streaming adjustments: streaming responses will be charged with the same band but allow a clocked grace window for handshake/keepalive noise. 3) Telemetry and sampling: roll experiment to 10% of eligible orgs (self-serve customers >30k monthly tokens but no Reserved contracts), holdback for customers with existing credits. 4) SQ harmonization: update Security Questionnaire (enterprise-SQ) language to transparently describe billing flow, token accounting, audit logs, and reconciliation data we can provide (structured billing export, per-request token trace IDs, KMS/HSM encryption controls).

Primary metrics: billing disputes (counts and time-to-resolution), net revenue delta, session latency P95, percent of sessions hitting per-session minimum, NPS delta for trial cohort. Secondary metrics: number of legal/SQ follow-ups, support ticket volume tagged "billing-io", and churn for pilot customers.

Success criteria (experimental guardrails): no >2% regression in latency P95 for streaming endpoints; billing disputes reduced >=30% at 90 days; net revenue impact within +/-5% versus control after smoothing credits.

Edge cases considered: multi-tenant bursts (long outputs with small inputs), batch tokenization differences across SDK versions, and incomplete GRPC stream commits resulting in mis-attributed tokens. We will normalize token counts using server-side canonical tokenizer and discard SDK-side token headers for billing.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment config defined and validated in console: parity band parameter, per-session minimum cap, streaming grace window

Legal and Security questionnaire updates drafted and reviewed by Security & Legal, and sample billing exports attached
Pilot rolled to 10% of eligible self-serve accounts and monitoring dashboards onboarded

2026-03-05: Security review kickoff. Security team requested explicit sample CSV schema and retention policy for per-request token traces. Added security_review_required flag. Internal SQ draft: https://drive.google.com/file/d/SEC_QA_DRAFT_PM353210

2026-03-08: Revenue Ops sanity check — simulated billing run across 50 customer billing snapshots shows estimated net revenue delta of +0.9% with current band parameter. Shared sandbox dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/pm353210/billing-probe
2026-03-10: PM retrospective note — shortened grace window for streaming to 2s after load testing to avoid latency regressions. Preparing canary rollout to 10% starting 2026-03-15.
notes: We should coordinate with the Dedicated team to ensure parity band logic can be represented consistently in contracts for customers who later move to Reserved capacity.
Consider an automatic reconciliation export that customers can opt into for their first billing cycle after rollout to reduce disputes.
If disputes persist beyond 15 days for pilot customers, pause experiment for that org and open a dedicated escalation channel with Revenue Ops.
